original.target_description: Hsee (1998), Study 1: between-subject comparison of perceived gift-giver generosity for a $45 wool scarf versus a $55 wool coat; Midwestern university students; reported t test.

n.quote: Respondents were 83 students from a large Midwestern university
n.sample_role: Student participants in the two-condition Study 1 comparison; no separate condition counts printed here.
n.exclusions: No exclusions reported in Study 1; analytic sample identified from the study-specific respondents and sole reported comparison.

replication.target_description: Vonasch et al. (2023), Replication of Study 1, gift scenario: separate evaluations of perceived generosity for a $45 scarf versus a $55 coat, American MTurk participants; Welch t test. Joint evaluation extension excluded from target.

n.location: Replication of Study 1: The Gift scenario, condition descriptions; Participants section
n.quote: Coat condition presented a coat on the lower end of a $50- $500 price range (N = 135): [...] The Scarf condition was similar, but instead of a coat they were given a scarf which was on the higher end of a much lower price range $5 to $50 (N = 131):
n.sample_role: Participants assigned to the two separate-evaluation conditions used in the target generosity comparison; printed condition counts retained separately.
n.exclusions: Three of 403 recruited participants excluded for refusing participation, leaving 400 across all conditions. No additional Study 1 exclusions reported; joint condition is outside this comparison.

notes: Original full paper title and author verified against supplied reference. Original PDF text extraction renders decimal points as colons and equals signs as an encoding artifact; numeric values transcribed from those printed statistics without metric conversion, with raw cached quote retained. Replication primary publisher HTML title and authors verified. Requested test-statistic metric retained for each side. Replication narrative rounds Welch df to 223; Table 1 gives 222.87 for the same generosity test. Replication also prints d = 0.99, 95% CI [0.72, 1.25]; this does not replace requested t. Replication n contains the two printed condition counts rather than the generic 400-participant sample. Replication locator p.3 resolved by named Study 1 section and Table 1 in HTML; page numbering not asserted.
